completion_definition: Completed means the initial curated cross-reference pass: the source verse and every listed target passage were read in the pinned Saints-Translation English records, and each retained pair has a specific explanation. It does not mean every possible biblical connection has been exhausted, or independent scholarly approval.

review_receipts.canon_authority: Repository canon.json, Saints Holy Bible seventy-book edition; all source and target books checked against it
review_receipts.second_editorial_pass: Completed. Reread explanations against actual English source/target text and necessary context; no retained missing target or self-containing range.

editorial_notes.note: Isaac's old age and uncertainty about death are not made into an assertion that he dies immediately; his actual death and age are recorded later at35:28-29.
Before the Lord is retained as part of Rebekah's reported wording; it is not inserted into the narrator's earlier version of Isaac's request.

The feared contempt/curse language and Rebekah's taking the curse upon herself are preserved. No later curse on Rebekah is invented. The source's arms and later hands wording is not independently reconstructed through a new Greek collation.
Jacob's identity and providence claims remain his speech. The actual food-preparation narrative and Isaac's later deceit description are not turned into divine endorsement of the impersonation.

The earlier service oracle and later Edomite revolt are compared in their actual settings. The yoke-release saying is not assigned an exhaustive historical date or forced into another translation's restless wording.

Esau's accusation about the birthright is distinguished from Genesis25's actual sale account. The later repentance/tears wording is retained without settling its psychological or grammatical alternatives. Isaac's being deeply moved at27:38 is preserved.
The supplied blessing to Esau positively says of the richness of the earth and of the dew. It is not replaced by an away-from-fertility reading.

The original fragment ending until the fury remains a separate verse unit completed by45. The few-days expectation is compared with Jacob's later twenty years, without invented travel dates or an unreported summons from Rebekah.
The source says my God in the blessing and retains the actual Bethuel/Laban family titles. No different divine name or independent genealogy harmonization is inserted.
Mahalath and Basemath are compared through the shared Ishmael/Nebaioth relationship while both supplied names remain intact. No unsupported renaming theory or single reconciled wife list is asserted.

John's angels-ascending/descending saying is retained as imagery reuse; it does not contain the word ladder. The source's Lord stood firm upon it is not silently replaced by above him. No claim about the sole source of Hebrews13:5 or eventual divine abandonment after fulfilment is made.

House of God/Oulamlous and the later Luz/Bethel forms are preserved through the narrative's explicit return-and-appearance recollections, without a new etymology. Pillars, oil, vow, altar and tenth are distinguished; no unreported constructed temple is claimed.

post_review_corrections.correction: Used passive wording about the grandsons being brought near to avoid assigning Joseph's action to Jacob; context in Genesis 48:9,13 identifies the request and the bringing.

editorial_notes.note: Laban is identified through the supplied Rebekah/Bethuel/Nahor family sequence. Son-of-Nahor and bone-and-flesh language are compared without erasing an intermediate generation or confusing kinship with the spousal relationship in Genesis2:23. No exact identification of the two well sites or city labels is newly established.
Leah's eyes remain weak in the supplied text. No medical diagnosis or conclusion that she was unattractive is imposed. Jacob's love and service proposal are quoted on their own terms.

Laban's older-before-younger explanation is his reported local-practice claim, not an independently verified universal custom. The week, Rachel's giving and the additional seven years retain their stated sequence; Rachel is not made to wait until the second seven-year term ends.
The deceit comparison identifies the language of Isaac's earlier statement and Jacob's later accusation. It does not invent a narrator's declaration of divine retribution.

Unequal love, hatred, jealousy and naming explanations remain attributed to the narrator or individual speakers as supplied. No universal moral verdict is inferred from a woman's fertility or barrenness. Biological mother and household naming speaker remain distinct for Bilhah and Zilpah's sons.
The supplied Samuel account describes Hannah's distress and the Lord's closing her womb; no familiar alternate wording about Peninnah provoking her is imported.

Sara's earlier request and Rachel's request are compared as household arrangements while retaining their different supplied wording. The links do not add a divine approval of every human choice or modern legal classifications.

God judged in my favour, God helped me, Good fortune, women calling blessed, Reward, a good gift and the request for another son retain their particular supplied wording and speakers. No independent original-language etymological collation or unreported divine oracle is claimed.
Later blessing and reproach-removal language is compared thematically. Luke is not asserted to quote Leah or Rachel explicitly, and the women's situations remain distinct.

Mandrake fruit and the sisters' exchange are retained as narrative details. The narrator says God heard Leah; no scientific or medicinal fertility effect of the plants is asserted, nor is Leah's reward interpretation made into an unreported divine verdict.

The later accounts of service, wages and wealth remain Jacob's and his wives' reported perspectives where appropriate. The supplied Genesis31:7 and41 wording concerns wages of ten lambs/ewe lambs; it is not silently replaced with a familiar ten-times wording. Laban's divining-by-signs claim is not endorsed as a method.

Grey lambs and the white-marked/spotted goat terms are preserved alongside the distinct formulations in the later dream report. Styrax, walnut and plane-tree rods retain the supplied botanical labels without new species identification. The procedure and coloured births are reported as narrative sequence, not demonstrated scientific efficacy.
The supplied contrast is rod placement while mating/conceiving versus no placement when sheep gave birth. Strong-versus-weak or selective-fitness wording from another edition is not substituted.

The supplied doubled exceedingly and the livestock/oxen/household catalogue are retained in the source text. Laban's sons' later accusation and Jacob's crediting God are kept as reported perspectives rather than a new independent verdict about the transactions.

candidate_exclusions.reason: The supplied Joseph wording is Do not fear, for I belong to God. A proposed identical Am I in the place of God phrase comparison was not retained.

review_receipts.second_editorial_pass: completed against all 148 distinct actual target verse texts; supplied variants and narrator-versus-character claims preserved

editorial_notes.note: Genesis 31 has53 supplied verse units: no separate31:51 or31:55. Genesis 32 has33 units and begins with Laban's morning farewell. Exact labels/anchors are retained, including the wrestling at32:25 and the thigh custom at32:33.

The sons' accusation, Jacob's divine-transfer and service claims, the daughters' inheritance complaint, and Laban's ownership/captivity allegations remain differing reported perspectives. The review does not supply an independent legal judgment or convert all speeches into narrator-verified facts.
Retain wages of ten lambs and wages of ten ewe lambs. These readings are not silently changed to ten times or ten wage changes.

The particular English coat-marking categories and dream descriptions remain intact. Narrative correspondences do not claim a verified modern breeding mechanism or force every conditional wage category into identical wording.
The pillar and vow are expressly recalled, while the supplied place-of-God naming remains visible. No new original-language etymology or location identification is claimed.

Rachel's theft, concealment and claim about her customary condition are distinguished from Jacob's ignorance. Her stated condition is not independently diagnosed. No inheritance motive for the idols, causal link to her later death, or identification of the stolen objects with every later buried god is established.
The actual warning is not to speak evil to Jacob. It is not silently expanded to another edition's good-or-bad formulation.
Retain the supplied search order: Leah, Jacob, the two slave women, then Rachel. No familiar alternate ordering is substituted.

Jacob's shepherding defense is compared with the actual later law about stolen versus wild-animal losses. It does not make Jacob subject to Sinai legislation or claim that the source says he paid for every wild-animal loss. Paul's hardship list and David's predator-rescue account are qualified comparisons, not identical occupations or actions.

The supplied English heap names and The Watch are retained without invented language derivations. References to God as witness, ancestral-God titles and the no-one-with-us wording are preserved without a forced resolution alongside the present kinsmen. The two meal notices are not independently adjudicated as separate events or one recapitulated event.
Encampments remains the supplied place name. Angelic-camp/guarding Psalms are thematic comparisons and do not identify individual angels or declare a modern site.

Esau approaches with four hundred men; these passages do not say they are armed attackers. Jacob's feared assault is distinguished from the later embrace, and the different camp/family arrangements are not equated.

The prayer says all the righteousness and truth shown suffice for Jacob, not a substituted unworthy-of-the-least wording. Preserve sea-sand here beside earth-sand at28:14 and seashore-sand in the ancestral oath, without forcing verbatim identity.
Retain eleven children. No reconstructed gender-specific or complete household census is imposed to replace the supplied count.

Genesis initially calls the wrestler a man; Jacob interprets the encounter as seeing God; Hosea speaks of prevailing with God and an angel. These descriptions remain visible without an independent ontological identification, Christological equation or forced harmonization. Hosea's later plural they-wept wording is not turned into a fresh claim that Genesis narrates Jacob weeping.

Retain the thigh becoming numb, the subsequent limp and the narrated sinew-food custom. No replacement with a different injury description, medical diagnosis, or assertion of later Sinai origin is made.

The name question is compared with Jacob's earlier Esau claim without declaring a full repentance interpretation. Form of God remains the supplied place name. Comparisons with Exodus 33:20 and Esau's face at33:10 do not independently reconcile the divine-face texts or identify Esau as God.

editorial_notes.note: Jacob explicitly compares seeing Esau with seeing the face of God. The comparison is retained without identifying Esau as God.

Retain the proposed Seir visit and subsequent distinct routes to Seir and Booths. No unreported later visit is supplied. The source calls the arrival place Salem, a city of Shechem; no identification with Jerusalem is asserted.

Genesis gives Hamor and a hundred lambs; Joshua gives the Amorites and one hundred ewe lambs. Preserve both supplied descriptions. Genesis 34:2 calls Shechem a Horite; this is not silently changed to a familiar alternative.

Shechem's subsequent attachment and marriage offer do not undo the narrated violation. Circumcision in the deceptive agreement is not a divine command to retaliate. Later rebukes of Simeon and Levi remain linked alongside the brothers' own defense.

The return account uses Luz and Bethel; the earlier account supplies House of God and Oulamlous. Keep the exact supplied forms without silently substituting names or reconstructing their linguistic relationship.

Deborah is Rebekah's nurse here and is not identified with another Deborah. The pinned inventory has no Genesis 35:21 unit; the tower of Gader occurs within 35:16. Preserve the existing source inventory and do not manufacture the missing verse.

Keep the dying mother's supplied Son of My Sorrow and the father's Benjamin. The collective Mesopotamia-of-Syria summary in verse26 remains quoted alongside Benjamin's birth journey near Ephrath in verses16-18; no geographic harmonization is imposed.
The association concerns Rachel and Bethlehem. Matthew quotes Jeremiah; it does not quote Genesis 35:19 as its prophecy.

findings.issue: The rationale unnecessarily assigns bringing the descendants near to Jacob. The target has an unnamed he, and the read context has Jacob asking Joseph to bring them (48:9) and Joseph bringing them (48:13). Preserve the narrative parallel while avoiding an ambiguous actor assignment.
findings.current_rationale: Jacob later likewise has eyes dim with age and brings descendants near for blessing, providing a generational parallel to Isaac's failing sight.
findings.requested_rationale: Jacob later likewise has eyes dim with age as his grandsons are brought near to him for blessing, providing a generational parallel to Isaac's failing sight.

critical_checks: Jacob's impersonation and his invoking the Lord over the food remain distinct from the narrator's account of Rebekah's preparation. Isaac's retrospective deceit statement is attributed to Isaac.
Esau's accusation concerning the birthright is compared with the narrated sale/despising and Hebrews12:16 without substituting the accusation for narration.
Rebekah's curse offer is not asserted to have been fulfilled; her hoped-for short absence and Esau forgetting are not claimed as narrated outcomes.
Hebrews11:20 interprets Isaac's future blessing as faith without blessing the deceptive method. Hebrews12:17 repentance wording is not doctrinally resolved beyond the supplied evidence.
Genesis27:39 retains positive earth-richness/dew wording. Genesis27:40 comparison with Edom's later revolt is labelled historical comparison, not exhaustive fulfilment.
Esau is explicitly Edom in read context Genesis36:1,8. The Judah revolt context identifies the king of Judah and is not confused with the same-named contemporary king of Israel.
Mahalath in28:9 and Basemath in36:3 remain different supplied names with shared kinship description; no invented renaming or harmonization is asserted.
Genesis28:13 includes Do not fear in this supplied edition. Genesis13:16 and28:14 use sand; familiar alternate wording is not imported.
House of God/Oulamlous in28:19 and Luz/Bethel in35:6-7 retain their own wording; the local naming variation is not silently corrected.
John1:51 is an imagery-reuse link: angels ascend/descend upon the Son of Man, and John does not say ladder.
Pillar, oil, altar and vow links do not assert a constructed temple or an unreported completed tithe. Hebrews7:1-10 was read as context confirming Abraham as the earlier tenth-giver.
All147 retained targets resolve in Saints70; no duplicate or self-containing source-target pair was found.

editorial_findings.finding: The Bethuel/Nahor sequence is not flattened. The earlier Laban is supported by Rebekah-brother identification, and the well accounts are compared without claiming a newly proven identical location. Bone/flesh language is qualified to keep marriage and nephew kinship distinct.

Weak eyes is preserved without diagnosis or an added verdict about Leah's appearance. The seven-year terms and week-before-Rachel sequence remain distinct. Laban's local custom and Jacob's deception charge remain attributed character statements; no divine retribution is invented.

Motherhood, household affiliation and the woman speaking the naming words remain distinct, particularly for Bilhah and Zilpah. The later genealogy actually names the retained children and their mothers. The Hannah and Luke links use the supplied wording and qualified contrasts; no familiar Peninnah-provocation text is imported.

The mandrake exchange is connected to the ensuing household agreement and birth while God's hearing Leah remains the narrator's account. The rationales do not claim verified plant efficacy or turn Leah's reward explanation into a separate divine verdict.

Laban's divination language, Jacob's service/prosperity account and Laban's sons' subsequent accusation remain attributed. The later Genesis 31:41 evidence uses wages of ten ewe lambs, not an imported ten-times reading. Grey/marked flock terms and pronouns are not forced into additional unreported intentions.

The actual styrax/walnut/plane rods, watering, conception, birth and colour accounts are used. Verse 42 says no placement when sheep gave birth; neither it nor its explanation imports a strong-versus-weak selection account. Retrospective dream parallels remain interpretive narrative connections rather than independently verified biology.

Every rationale identifies a particular textual, genealogical or literary connection. Same-chapter pairs concern explained identities, proposal/response, stated agreements, repetitions or narrated consequences. All references resolve in the supplied source inventory, the full target text hashes match the author receipt, all books are within Saints70, and there are no duplicate or self-containing pairs.

findings.problem: The rationale calls the appeal to the townsmen private, although Genesis34:20 explicitly locates this speech at the city gate before the men of their city. It is a different audience, but the text does not describe a private conversation.
findings.action: Keep the pair and relationship; replace the rationale.
findings.recommended_rationale: The earlier invitation promises Jacob's family room to acquire possessions; the later appeal to their own townsmen anticipates acquiring Jacob's property, showing the proposal from the other side.

findings.problem: Both passages concern Jacob's practical arrangements for his livestock during the same journey, so the association is useful. However, the report of making booths does not expressly say the nursing animals caused the choice to settle at Booths.
findings.action: The pair may remain; label it as an association and avoid inferred causation.
findings.recommended_rationale: Jacob previously explains that the nursing herds require a slower pace; the later report that he makes booths for his livestock supplies another practical provision for those animals during the journey, without stating that their condition caused his settlement there.

confirmed_distinctions: Source35:21 is absent and has not been manufactured or counted. The tower of Gader remains within source35:16; the collective Mesopotamia wording in35:26 is not harmonized away.
Source33:18 says Salem, a city of Shechem; no proposed link identifies that city with Jerusalem or Melchizedek's Salem.

Source33:19 has Hamor and100 lambs; Joshua24:32 names the Amorites and100 ewe lambs. The rationale retains the supplied seller difference rather than silently harmonizing it. The Ephron/Double Cave purchase is only a distinct patriarchal land-purchase parallel.
Source34:2 says Horite. None of the rationales substitutes a different ethnicity.
The Shechem/Tamar comparisons retain the assaults and contrast the men's later responses without making affection, payment, proposed marriage or retaliation an excuse or divine authorization.
The circumcision comparisons distinguish the covenant sign from the sons' deceitful use of it; later legal comparisons do not claim that Shechem's conduct is identical to Exodus22:15-16.
The source35:4 account includes both hiding and destroying the household objects; the proposed links do not restrict all objects to Rachel or erase the supplied actions.
Oulamlous/House of God at28:19 and Luz/Bethel at35:6 remain supplied forms, without an invented place-name etymology or silent spelling correction.
The pillars connected with divine appearances and Rachel's grave are explicitly distinguished in purpose. Deborah's Oak of Mourning is a separate death memorial.

Matthew2:16-18 is a later maternal-lament association. Its Jeremiah quotation names Ramah; the source is Rachel's burial on the road to Bethlehem. The rationale neither identifies the sites nor claims Genesis35:19 is Matthew's quoted prophecy.
The genealogy links preserve distinct maternal branches, Benjamin's supplied descendants, and the source's difficult collective birthplace summary without adding a harmonization.
Source35:29 and25:8-9 are comparable death-and-two-sons-burial narratives;49:31 supplies the later cave identification. Isaac's earlier old age is not treated as his immediate death.
